# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## plugin:deepwork:deepwork
## Available Workflows

This project uses DeepWork. If the user wants to do something matching these, use `/deepwork` to start the workflow.

- **deepplan** (create_deep_plan): Structured planning workflow that produces an executable DeepWork job definition
- **deepwork_jobs** (new_job, repair, learn, shared_jobs): Creates and manages multi-step AI workflows. Use when defining, implementing, testing, or improving DeepWork jobs.
- **deepwork_reviews** (discover_rules, add_document_update_rule): Manage .deepreview rules for automated code review

# DeepWork Workflow Server

Multi-step workflows with quality gates.

**Session identity**: On Claude Code pass `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` as `session_id`. On other platforms omit `session_id` in `start_workflow`; the server auto-generates one and returns it in `begin_step.session_id` — use that value for all subsequent calls. Sub-agents on Claude Code also pass `agent_id` (CLAUDE_CODE_AGENT_ID).

## Workflow Lifecycle

1. `get_workflows` — discover available workflows
2. `start_workflow` — begin with goal, job_name, workflow_name (session_id optional — see above)
3. Follow step instructions; use `begin_step.session_id` for all subsequent calls, then call `finished_step` with outputs
4. If `needs_work`: fix issues and retry. If `next_step`: continue. If `workflow_complete`: done.

Workflows nest via stack. Use `abort_workflow` to cancel, `go_to_step` to revisit earlier steps.

?? bench/diff_duplicates_precision.jsonl
## Study 10: would a diff-scoped "you re-implemented an existing function" finding be right?

[`archy duplicates`](../README.md) reports the duplication backlog of a whole tree. A
reviewer asks something narrower at change time: did this diff add a function that
already exists? Keeping only the clusters with one member in the diff's added lines and
one that already existed at base would turn the report into that check
([#548](https://github.com/hslee16/archy/issues/548)). Two earlier detectors that looked
obviously useful had missed their precision bars (Study 7 at 0.024 against 0.70, Study 9
at 0.215 against 0.40), so this one was measured before anything was built.

**Pre-registered before the harness existed**
([`research/DIFF_DUPLICATES_PRECISION.md`](research/DIFF_DUPLICATES_PRECISION.md)):
a headroom kill below 1 firing per 50 Python agent PRs or below 30 scorable firings from
10 repos; precision pass at 0.60 and kill below 0.40 under two blind labelers; and no
post-hoc subgroup rescue of a null or a kill.

**Headroom passed. Precision did not.** Over 2,000 sampled AIDev PRs, 1,049 were
measurable Python PRs and 177 of them (16.9%) produced a firing, 557 firings in 134
repos. Of 119 firings labeled blind by two models, **19 were true under the strict
reading (both labelers), 0.160, and 33 under the lenient one, 0.277**, both below the
0.40 kill line. The finding is not built.

The false firings are mostly not bugs in the detector so much as the wall Studies 7 and
9 hit: shape does not say why. The reasons the labelers gave were short functions that
clear 30 nodes, a shape repeated so widely that there is no single "existing one" to
reuse, and per-backend or per-format siblings. Near-miss (the Type-3 tier) supplied 348
of the 557 firings and was the least precise, 10 of 76. The exact tier was 4 of 10, which
is a subgroup on ten firings, reported and not counted.

Three things to hold next to the number. **No human labeled:** the second labeler was
changed from me to a second model before it ran, recorded in an addendum and
a ticket, so kappa 0.66 is model-to-model agreement and this is not human-validated. **Type-4
(semantic) redundancy, the kind the agent-PR literature measures, is not measured here**,
because this detector misses it by design. And **module-name collisions dropped 22% of
the Python PRs**, so the measured population may lean toward cleaner repositories; I did
not measure that.

Full results, including the git oracle (which could not confirm the labelers) and the
SonarQube-gate comparison, are in
[`../bench/diff_duplicates_precision_results.md`](../bench/diff_duplicates_precision_results.md).

## What survived, and why archy still exists

Two nulls on agent-side benefit, one retracted premise, a study saying the
problem is rare, and one modest positive whose size is set by how rarely the
problem occurs did not kill the tool, but between them they have narrowed what
I am allowed to claim about it almost to nothing. archy's README carries no
token-savings number, and a rule in `RESEARCH_METRICS.md` §14c.7 forbids adding
one. It carries no agent-safety number either, and after Experiment 3 it never
will.

What survived is a narrower and more defensible job. A competitive analysis I
ran against the most successful tool in the adjacent category found the
distinction is **descriptive versus normative**. Navigation-first graph tools
describe the structure that *exists*: what is here, what calls what. They are
better at that than archy is, and archy's README says so by name.

archy holds the structure you *declared*: layers, forbidden edges, an
acyclicity invariant, a recorded score baseline. That job needs user-supplied
intent, which is not recoverable from source code at any parsing quality. It is
the same wall the pattern-detection study hit from the inside: "domain" is a
statement of intent, and the import graph does not carry intent.

That analysis also concluded its own maintainer was working on the wrong thing.
9 of 11 archy tools had no counterpart in the competitor, so differentiation
     175 bench/diff_duplicates_precision_results.md
     302 docs/research/DIFF_DUPLICATES_PRECISION.md
     477 total

1	# Diff-scoped duplicates: firing rate and precision (#548)
2	
3	Captured 2026-11-11. Pre-registration:
4	[`docs/research/DIFF_DUPLICATES_PRECISION.md`](../docs/research/DIFF_DUPLICATES_PRECISION.md),
5	committed as `d1f60b45` on `main` (`7f132773` on its branch), BEFORE the harness
6	(`6119dffd`) existed. Three dated addenda follow it, each written before the thing it
7	describes ran or was read: after the pilot (`7d16093f`), during the run (`65d15650`),
8	and labeler A (`65d15650`, tracked in #959). Thresholds, the firing definition and the
9	rubric were never changed.
10	
11	## Verdict: precision kill. The finding is not built.
12	
13	| step | pre-registered bar | measured | result |
14	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
15	| Headroom: firing rate | at least 1 PR in 50 (2%) | 177 of 1,049 measured Python PRs, **16.9%** (13.0% if dropped Python PRs count as clean) | pass |
16	| Headroom: scorable firings and repos | at least 30 from at least 10 repos | 557 firings in 134 repos; **119 scorable from 66 repos** | pass |
17	| Precision, strict (both labelers TRUE) | pass at least 0.60, kill below 0.40 | **19 of 119 = 0.160** | **kill** |
18	
19	The lenient reading (either labeler TRUE) is 33 of 119 = 0.277, also below 0.40, so the
20	choice between the two readings does not matter here. Cohen's kappa between the two
21	labelers is 0.66.
22	
23	By the pre-registration this is a result, not "try again", and no subgroup rescues it.
24	
25	## The limitation that has to sit beside the number
26	
27	**No human label exists.** Both labelers are LLMs (A `claude-sonnet-5-5`, B
28	`claude-opus-5-5`), a deviation recorded in addendum 3 before the second labeler ran and
29	tracked in #959. Models from one vendor share training lineage, so shared blind spots
30	are likelier than between a person and a model, and kappa 0.66 is model-to-model
31	agreement only. This result is not human-validated. For a human to move it out of the
32	kill zone, they would have to call at least 48 of the 119 firings true, against 33 for
33	the more generous of the two models, so it is unlikely to change the verdict, but it
34	has not been shown.
35	
36	Three of labeler B's 119 labels were printed during an end-to-end check before that
37	decision (disclosed in addendum 3). They were not used to choose the model, the second
38	labeler or any threshold.
39	
40	## Population and headroom
41	
42	2,000 PRs drawn from 57,517 closed AIDev PRs in Python-language repositories (seed 548,
43	at most 25 per repo, pilot excluded). 87 ran in one process, the rest in 8 workers
44	sharded by repository.
45	
46	| | PRs |
47	| --- | ---: |
48	| drawn | 2,000 |
49	| no added Python line (never a Python PR) | 642 |
50	| dropped on `QualnameCollisionError` | 299 |
51	| unresolvable (repo or pull ref gone) | 8 |
52	| scan too large | 2 |
53	| analysis timeout | 0 |
54	| **measured Python PRs** | **1,049** |
55	| with at least one firing | 177 |
56	
57	557 firings; median 2 per firing PR, largest 39. The top five repos supply 24% of them
58	and the per-repo cap held (at most 24 measured PRs in one repo, 551 repos measured), so
59	this is not a one-repo artifact. Firing PRs by agent, over that agent's measured PRs:
60	Claude Code 106 of 538, Copilot 25 of 199, Codex 34 of 228, Cursor 7 of 24, Devin 3 of
61	36, Jules 2 of 24.
62	
63	**Attrition may fall unevenly.** The 299 collision drops are archy refusing trees where
64	two files share a module name. In the pilot those were large repositories (prefect,
65	mlflow, nexus); I did not measure repository size across all 299, so that the measured
66	population leans toward smaller, cleaner repositories is a suspicion, not a finding.
67	Counting all 309 dropped Python PRs as clean gives the 13.0% figure. Neither moves the
68	headroom result.
69	
70	**Near-miss supplies most firings and is least precise.** 348 of the 557 are near-miss
71	(Type-3, the 0.85 token-overlap tier). 16 firings are in PRs where the shipped near-miss
72	pass hit its 5,000,000-comparison budget and may be short.
73	
74	## Primary oracle: two blind labelers
75	
76	120 firings drawn by seeded sample from the 557 (seed 548) over ids alone, before any
77	packet was built. 119 packets were built; one firing could not be read at the head
78	commit and is dropped as unscorable, never scored FALSE. No firing was marked
79	UNSCORABLE by either labeler.
80	
81	| | TRUE | of | precision |
82	| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
83	| strict (both TRUE) | 19 | 119 | 0.160 |
84	| lenient (either TRUE) | 33 | 119 | 0.277 |
85	
86	Why the rest are FALSE (each labeler's reason, frozen rubric):
87	
88	| reason | A | B |
89	| --- | ---: | ---: |
90	| short-or-trivial | 23 | 19 |
91	| widespread-name | 19 | 16 |
92	| sibling | 17 | 24 |
93	| example-or-test-like | 10 | 14 |
94	| other | 9 | 15 |
95	| boilerplate | 5 | 9 |
96	| isolation | 2 | 1 |
97	| same-class | 1 | 2 |
98	
99	Most of what fires is something a person would call intended or too small to matter:
100	short functions that clear 30 nodes, the same shape repeated so widely that there is no
101	single "existing one" to reuse, and per-backend or per-format siblings.
102	
103	## Subgroups (reported in full, never results)
104	
105	| group | strict TRUE | lenient TRUE | firings |
106	| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
107	| exact (byte-identical body) | 4 | 7 | 10 |
108	| shape-identical, not byte-identical | 5 | 6 | 33 |
109	| near-miss | 10 | 20 | 76 |
110	| copy in a new file | 13 | 20 | 78 |
111	| copy in an existing file | 6 | 13 | 41 |
112	
113	The exact tier is 4 of 10 strict, which sits at the kill line, on ten firings. It is not
114	a result: the pre-registration names exact versus near-miss as a subgroup to be
115	reported in full and never counted, forbids a post-hoc subgroup rescue, and an interval
116	on n=10 is far wider than any bar. A follow-up that wanted an exact-only finding would need its own
117	pre-registration and its own sample.
118	
119	## Secondary: the git oracle (never decisive)
120

# Diff-scoped duplicates: firing rate and precision (#548)

Captured 2026-11-11. Pre-registration:
[`docs/research/DIFF_DUPLICATES_PRECISION.md`](../docs/research/DIFF_DUPLICATES_PRECISION.md),
committed as `d1f60b45` on `main` (`7f132773` on its branch), BEFORE the harness
(`6119dffd`) existed. Three dated addenda follow it, each written before the thing it
describes ran or was read: after the pilot (`7d16093f`), during the run (`65d15650`),
and labeler A (`65d15650`, tracked in #959). Thresholds, the firing definition and the
rubric were never changed.

## Verdict: precision kill. The finding is not built.

| step | pre-registered bar | measured | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Headroom: firing rate | at least 1 PR in 50 (2%) | 177 of 1,049 measured Python PRs, **16.9%** (13.0% if dropped Python PRs count as clean) | pass |
| Headroom: scorable firings and repos | at least 30 from at least 10 repos | 557 firings in 134 repos; **119 scorable from 66 repos** | pass |
| Precision, strict (both labelers TRUE) | pass at least 0.60, kill below 0.40 | **19 of 119 = 0.160** | **kill** |

The lenient reading (either labeler TRUE) is 33 of 119 = 0.277, also below 0.40, so the
choice between the two readings does not matter here. Cohen's kappa between the two
labelers is 0.66.

By the pre-registration this is a result, not "try again", and no subgroup rescues it.

## The limitation that has to sit beside the number

**No human label exists.** Both labelers are LLMs (A `claude-sonnet-5-5`, B
`claude-opus-5-5`), a deviation recorded in addendum 3 before the second labeler ran and
tracked in #959. Models from one vendor share training lineage, so shared blind spots
are likelier than between a person and a model, and kappa 0.66 is model-to-model
agreement only. This result is not human-validated. For a human to move it out of the
kill zone, they would have to call at least 48 of the 119 firings true, against 33 for
the more generous of the two models, so it is unlikely to change the verdict, but it
has not been shown.

Three of labeler B's 119 labels were printed during an end-to-end check before that
decision (disclosed in addendum 3). They were not used to choose the model, the second
labeler or any threshold.

## Population and headroom

2,000 PRs drawn from 57,517 closed AIDev PRs in Python-language repositories (seed 548,
at most 25 per repo, pilot excluded). 87 ran in one process, the rest in 8 workers
sharded by repository.

| | PRs |
| --- | ---: |
| drawn | 2,000 |
| no added Python line (never a Python PR) | 642 |
| dropped on `QualnameCollisionError` | 299 |
| unresolvable (repo or pull ref gone) | 8 |
| scan too large | 2 |
| analysis timeout | 0 |
| **measured Python PRs** | **1,049** |
| with at least one firing | 177 |

557 firings; median 2 per firing PR, largest 39. The top five repos supply 24% of them
and the per-repo cap held (at most 24 measured PRs in one repo, 551 repos measured), so
this is not a one-repo artifact. Firing PRs by agent, over that agent's measured PRs:
Claude Code 106 of 538, Copilot 25 of 199, Codex 34 of 228, Cursor 7 of 24, Devin 3 of
36, Jules 2 of 24.

**Attrition may fall unevenly.** The 299 collision drops are archy refusing trees where
two files share a module name. In the pilot those were large repositories (prefect,
mlflow, nexus); I did not measure repository size across all 299, so that the measured
population leans toward smaller, cleaner repositories is a suspicion, not a finding.
Counting all 309 dropped Python PRs as clean gives the 13.0% figure. Neither moves the
headroom result.

**Near-miss supplies most firings and is least precise.** 348 of the 557 are near-miss
(Type-3, the 0.85 token-overlap tier). 16 firings are in PRs where the shipped near-miss
pass hit its 5,000,000-comparison budget and may be short.

## Primary oracle: two blind labelers

120 firings drawn by seeded sample from the 557 (seed 548) over ids alone, before any
packet was built. 119 packets were built; one firing could not be read at the head
commit and is dropped as unscorable, never scored FALSE. No firing was marked
UNSCORABLE by either labeler.

| | TRUE | of | precision |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| strict (both TRUE) | 19 | 119 | 0.160 |
| lenient (either TRUE) | 33 | 119 | 0.277 |

Why the rest are FALSE (each labeler's reason, frozen rubric):

| reason | A | B |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| short-or-trivial | 23 | 19 |
| widespread-name | 19 | 16 |
| sibling | 17 | 24 |
| example-or-test-like | 10 | 14 |
| other | 9 | 15 |
| boilerplate | 5 | 9 |
| isolation | 2 | 1 |
| same-class | 1 | 2 |

Most of what fires is something a person would call intended or too small to matter:
short functions that clear 30 nodes, the same shape repeated so widely that there is no
single "existing one" to reuse, and per-backend or per-format siblings.

## Subgroups (reported in full, never results)

| group | strict TRUE | lenient TRUE | firings |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| exact (byte-identical body) | 4 | 7 | 10 |
| shape-identical, not byte-identical | 5 | 6 | 33 |
| near-miss | 10 | 20 | 76 |
| copy in a new file | 13 | 20 | 78 |
| copy in an existing file | 6 | 13 | 41 |

The exact tier is 4 of 10 strict, which sits at the kill line, on ten firings. It is not
a result: the pre-registration names exact versus near-miss as a subgroup to be
reported in full and never counted, forbids a post-hoc subgroup rescue, and an interval
on n=10 is far wider than any bar. A follow-up that wanted an exact-only finding would need its own
pre-registration and its own sample.

## Secondary: the git oracle (never decisive)

1	# Pre-registration: does a diff-scoped "re-implemented an existing function" finding fire often enough, and is it right when it fires? (#548)
2	
3	Written 2026-11-11, BEFORE `bench/diff_duplicates_precision.py` exists, before any PR was
4	drawn, and before any label was read. Edits after this date go in a dated addendum at the
5	bottom, never over this text. The commit that adds this file is quoted in the results.
6	
7	## Question
8	
9	`archy duplicates` reports the duplication backlog of a whole tree. A reviewer asks a
10	narrower thing at change time: did this diff add a function that already exists elsewhere?
11	Keeping only the clusters with one member inside the diff's added lines and one member that
12	already existed at the base commit would turn the report into that check. This study measures
13	two numbers on Python agent PRs before anything is built:
14	
15	1. **Firing rate:** how many PRs produce at least one such cluster.
16	2. **Precision:** of the firings, how many are cases where the new function should have
17	   called or reused the existing one.
18	
19	It measures the clones archy can see (AST-shape exact plus token-overlap near-miss). It does
20	not claim to cover Type-4 (semantic) redundancy, which is the kind the agent-PR literature
21	measures (arXiv 2601.21276) and which this detector misses by design. Low recall is expected
22	and is not a finding of this study.
23	
24	No agent time is spent. The unit of work is a git checkout and a parse, so the expensive part
25	of any bench here (live agent runs) does not apply.
26	
27	## The action, if it passes
28	
29	The PR author or the agent is told "new `f` in `a/x.py` matches existing `b/y.f`" and deletes
30	the copy in favour of a call. If the study fails, nothing is built and
31	`docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md` records why. This ticket ships no CLI flag, MCP parameter or hook,
32	is never a score input, and adds no embeddings and no per-turn hook output.
33	
34	## Prior art recorded before the run
35	
36	- **SonarQube Cloud, "Sonar way for agentic AI"** already fails a PR whose new code has more
37	  than 3% duplicated lines. A Python duplicated block there needs at least 100 successive
38	  duplicated tokens over at least 10 lines, with only indentation and string literals
39	  ignored, so a copy with renamed identifiers is not a duplicate to Sonar. archy folds
40	  identifiers and literals. The gate is a density threshold, so one 15-line copy in a
41	  600-line PR (2.5%) passes. See "Reported, never decisive" for what this study records
42	  about it.
43	- **mick-gsk/drift** ships the in-loop version as a Claude Code hook and measures its own
44	  speak-rate by replay (0.0% to 5.6% on five repos). Its first run said 27% to 69% and the
45	  output was junk; the classes it derived are enumerated below so they are counted as
46	  reasons for FALSE labels instead of tuned away after the fact. Its replay measures noise,
47	  not precision or effect, so it does not change the anti-theater answer for this ticket.
48	- Detector precision history: about 50% similarity-only ceiling, about 63% exact tier, about
49	  74% source with co-change demotion (#242, #247, `docs/LEARNINGS.md`). Co-change abstains
50	  for files with fewer than 5 commits (`min_evidence`), so a copy in a NEW file falls back
51	  toward the ceiling. This study is expected to land nearer 50% than 74% for that reason.
52	- Two shipped detectors missed their pre-registered precision bars: Study 7 (0.024 against
53	  0.70) and Study 9 (0.215 against 0.40). Both harness bugs in Study 7 produced
54	  publishable-looking numbers, which is why the canary below runs before any real run.
55	
56	## Population and sampling
57	
58	- **Source:** AIDev (`hao-li/AIDev`), tables `pull_request` (state, `merged_at`, `repo_url`,
59	  `agent`) and `pr_commit_details` (`filename`, `status`, `patch`, per commit). The base
60	  commit and head commit of each PR are recovered from the repository's git history, not
61	  from the dataset.
62	- **Python PR:** a PR with at least one `.py` file whose patch carries an added line. Merged
63	  and closed-unmerged PRs are both in; open PRs are out (no outcome and the head moves).
64	- **Pilot:** 20 Python PRs drawn with seed 548. The pilot is disjoint from the main sample
65	  by construction (drawn first, removed from the pool).
66	- **Main sample:** N Python PRs drawn uniformly at random from the remaining pool with seed
67	  548 and at most 25 PRs per repository (the cap stops one prolific repository from
68	  supplying the whole firing set; it is applied in draw order). N is fixed in the
69	  post-pilot addendum from the pilot's measured wall time per PR, and only from that. The
70	  sample is not extended after the run starts: a short result is a result.
71	- **Unmeasurable PRs are dropped, never scored clean.** A PR whose base or head cannot be
72	  checked out, whose tree fails to parse, or whose scan exceeds the module cap is recorded
73	  with its reason and removed from the denominator. Dropped counts are reported by reason,
74	  and the headroom rate is also reported with every dropped PR counted as a non-firing, so
75	  the effect of dropping is visible.
76	
77	## The detector and what counts as a firing
78	
79	The shipped detector, unmodified, run on the head tree:
80	
81	- exact clusters: `compute_duplicates(min_size=30)`, then `classify_variants`, then
82	  `demote_independent` where git history is present (the `archy duplicates` default);
83	- near-miss clusters: `compute_near_duplicates(min_size=30)` at the shipped 0.85 floor.
84	  These have no variant tier of their own, so the harness applies the same path filter
85	  (below) to them;
86	- **source-only (#247):** a cluster is dropped if any member is a test path
87	  (`is_test_path`) or a vendored path. Exact clusters the detector demotes to the `variant`
88	  tier are dropped. No other filter is added.
89	
90	A cluster is a **firing** iff both hold, computed from `git diff base..head`:
91	
92	- **A (new):** at least one member's `def` line falls inside an added hunk of the diff;
93	- **B (pre-existing):** at least one OTHER member existed at base, in a location outside the
94	  added hunks (a function present at base whose lines the diff did not add).
95	
96	One firing is one (PR, cluster) pair. The unit of precision is the firing. Firings in one PR
97	are reported both ways (per firing and per PR) so a single PR cannot hide behind a count.
98	Only clusters the diff touches can fire, so a backlog cluster wholly at base never counts.
99	
100	Headroom is `PRs with at least one firing / measured Python PRs`.
101	
102	## Oracles
103	
104	### Primary: blind labels from two labelers under the frozen rubric
105	
106	Each scorable firing is labelled by two labelers working independently. Each sees the
107	repository, the new function and the existing function (paths, bodies, surrounding file),
108	and is blind to: the detector tier and similarity, the PR's merge outcome, the reviewers'
109	comments, and the git oracle. They label each firing TRUE or FALSE, and for FALSE record one
110	reason from the list below.
111	
112	**TRUE** means: the new function should have called or reused the existing one (directly,
113	or by extracting a shared helper both call).
114	
115	**FALSE** means: the duplication is intended or benign.
116	
117	Frozen rubric for FALSE, one reason recorded per firing:
118	
119	| reason | meaning |
120	| --- | --- |
121	| `sibling` | per-backend, per-provider, per-version or per-format siblings that differ in ways the shape folds away |
122	| `boilerplate` | property shims, one-line delegation, dunder methods, argument-parsing scaffolds, CLI or schema glue |
123	| `example-or-test-like` | examples, docs, scripts, fixtures, migrations or generated code restating a name by design (including paths the harness did not recognise as test or vendored) |
124	| `isolation` | deliberate independence: vendored or forked code, a layer that must not import the other |
125	| `same-class` | symmetric methods of one class or one protocol |
126	| `widespread-name` | the same shape appears in many places as a convention, so no single "existing one" exists to reuse |
127	| `short-or-trivial` | too small for reuse to be worth a call, despite clearing 30 nodes |
128	| `other` | free text, which the labeller must write |
129	
130	A firing is **TRUE under the primary oracle only if both labelers say TRUE.** A split
131	decision is FALSE for the headline. The lenient reading (either says TRUE) is reported as
132	the upper bound and the strict reading as the headline; if they straddle a threshold, the
133	strict one decides. Cohen's kappa is reported with the counts. Labelers are recorded by
134	identity in the results; the labelling script reads nothing but the rubric and the two
135	functions.
136	
137	If the firing set exceeds 120, a seeded draw (seed 548) of 120 is labelled, before anything
138	else is read. Below that, every firing is labelled.
139	
140	**Firings that cannot be scored are dropped, never scored as clean.** A firing is
141	unscorable if either labeller cannot open the pre-existing member at its location, or the
142	two functions cannot be located at head. Drops are reported by reason.
143	
144	### Secondary, reported and never decisive: the git oracle
145	
146	A firing scores TRUE if the copy was removed or consolidated in a later revision of the same
147	PR or within 6 months on the default branch: the new function's qualified name is gone, or
148	its body no longer shares a shape with the existing member. The oracle is biased against the
149	feature, since reviewers do not object to redundant agent code (2601.21276), so it can only
150	under-count. It never decides a threshold.
151	
152	### Reported, never decisive: the Sonar comparison
153	
154	For each firing the primary oracle scores TRUE, record:
155	
156	1. whether the copy is at least 10 lines and identifier-identical (byte-identical concrete
157	   body, which is the `exact` tier);
158	2. the PR's new-code duplicated-line density from the same added hunks. This is a PROXY:
159	   duplicated lines are the added lines of functions that are members of kept clusters, over
160	   all added lines in `.py` files. It is not Sonar's 100-token, 10-line detector and is
161	   labelled as a proxy wherever it appears.
162	
163	If almost every TRUE firing would also have failed Sonar's 3% gate, the results say so,
164	because a follow-up feature would then add nothing for SonarQube users. The slice archy
165	alone would add is short copies, renamed copies, near-misses and copies diluted below 3% by
166	a large PR; any follow-up has to justify that slice. This adds no threshold.
167	
168	## Thresholds
169	
170	Fixed here, and not moved by the pilot or by anything read afterwards.
171	
172	- **Headroom kill:** fewer than 1 firing per 50 Python agent PRs in the main sample (a rate
173	  below 2%), OR fewer than 30 scorable firings from at least 10 repositories. Either means
174	  the feature is not built. This is a result, not "underpowered, try again."
175	- **Precision pass:** at least 0.60 over at least 30 scorable firings from at least 10
176	  repositories, under the primary oracle.
177	- **Precision kill:** below 0.40.
178	- **Between 0.40 and 0.60:** null, and not shipped.
179	
180	**No post-hoc subgroup rescues a null.** Exact versus near-miss, and new file versus
181	existing file, are reported in full, with counts and the reason breakdown, but they are not
182	results. The detector is not edited after the first labelled firing: the FALSE reasons above
183	are what a filter would have to remove, and removing them after seeing the labels would be
184	tuning on the test set.
185	
186	## Process, in order
187	
188	1. This document is committed. Its hash goes in the results.
189	2. The harness, the added-hunk unit tests (hand-built two-commit fixture; red when "member
190	   existed at base" is removed, red again when "def line inside an added hunk" is removed;
191	   the fixture asserts it contains a pre-existing match before asserting the outcome) and
192	   the canary.
193	3. `--canary`: a fixture PR that copies an existing function into a NEW file must fire, and a
194	   fixture PR that only edits an existing function must not. It runs before any real run.
195	4. Pilot on 20 disjoint PRs. **No labels are read.** It reports firing rate and harness bugs.
196	   A pilot of 20 expects well under one firing at a 2% rate, so it cannot estimate the rate
197	   and is a plumbing test only; the addendum says so. Its one design output is N, from
198	   wall time per PR.
199	5. Dated addendum fixing N, then the full run, resumable from the ledger (one row per PR,
200	   appended in a single write, only `status="ok"` counts as done, a crash in one PR does not
201	   end the run, stalls are retried and results never).
202	6. Labelling, then scoring against the thresholds, then
203	   `bench/diff_duplicates_precision_results.md` and a Study entry in
204	   `docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md`, published pass or fail.
205	
206	## Descriptive extra, not a threshold
207	
208	The headroom measurement already yields a speak-rate comparable to drift's replay numbers;
209	it is reported next to them so a reader can see whether archy would be noisier than the
210	in-loop tool that exists today.
211	
212	## Addenda
213	
214	### 2026-11-11, after the 20-PR pilot (no label read, no firing content read)
215	
216	Thresholds, the firing definition and the rubric are unchanged. What the pilot fixed or
217	revealed:
218	
219	- **Pilot result (counts only).** 20 PRs drawn, 7 measured, 9 had no added Python lines
220	  (dropped), 4 were dropped on `QualnameCollisionError`. 1 firing in 7 measured. As the
221	  plan said, this cannot estimate a rate near 2%; it is a plumbing test. Mean wall time was
222	  54 s per measured PR including cold clones. The pilot ledger is
223	  `bench/diff_duplicates_pilot.jsonl`; the pilot PRs are excluded from the main sample.
224	- **N = 2000.** The main sample is the 2000 PRs that follow the pilot in the seed-548
225	  shuffle, at most 25 per repository in draw order. About a third of draws are measurable
226	  in the pilot, so expect roughly 700 measured PRs; that expectation is an estimate from 20
227	  PRs and is not a commitment. The sample is not extended.
228	- **Pool is a proxy, the diff decides.** The draw pool is closed AIDev PRs in repositories
229	  whose AIDev `language` is Python (57,517 PRs in 4,255 repositories). A PR is a "Python
230	  PR" only if its own diff adds a `.py` line; the rest are dropped and recorded.
231	- **Diff base.** The base is `merge-base(PR base sha, PR head)`, the three-dot diff GitHub
232	  shows, so a PR branched long ago is not charged with unrelated base-branch changes. The
233	  head is the PR's `pull/N/head` ref.
234	- **Module-name collisions are dropped, not worked around.** 4 of the pilot's 11 Python PRs
235	  (prefect, mlflow, nexus and one more) hit `QualnameCollisionError`: archy refuses a tree
236	  where two files share a module name (#531), and the shipped CLI would refuse the same
237	  repositories. These are dropped and reported by reason, and the headroom rate is also
238	  reported with drops counted as non-firing. The results state plainly that this attrition
239	  falls on larger repositories, so the measured population leans toward smaller, cleaner
240	  ones. No fallback that ignores the colliding paths is added, since it would be a detector
241	  configuration the shipped CLI does not use.
242	- **Near-miss budget hits are flagged, not dropped.** The shipped near-miss pass stops at
243	  its 5,000,000-comparison budget and warns; at least one pilot repository hit it. A PR that
244	  hits it is still measured (the exact tier is complete) and its ledger row carries
245	  `near_miss_budget_hit`. The results report near-miss firings split by that flag, since a
246	  PR whose near-miss result may be short is not a clean negative for that tier.
247	- **Labelers.** Labeler A is the maintainer; labeler B is a fresh-context LLM given only
248	  the rubric and the two functions. Identities are recorded in the results.
249	
250	### 2026-11-11, during the main run and before any label was read
251	
252	Thresholds, the firing definition and the rubric are unchanged. Operational facts and two
253	clarifications, recorded before the results exist:
254	
255	- **Analysis timeout is a drop.** One PR's analysis is run in a supervised child with a
256	  30 minute wall ceiling. The ceiling was added mid-run after a shard sat for 22 minutes on
257	  `git log -M` (the co-change layer) over a blobless clone of a very large repository. A PR
258	  that hits it is dropped with the reason `analysis timeout`, counted among the dropped
259	  Python PRs in the second headroom figure (drops counted as clean), and never as a clean
260	  PR. The affected shards were restarted on that code and resumed from their ledgers.
261	- **The run was sharded by repository** (8 workers), after the first 87 PRs ran in one
262	  process. The draw is unchanged and a PR's result does not depend on its shard.
263	- **Labeler B reads more than the packet.** It is a fresh-context `claude -p` run per
264	  firing, with the packet (repository, the new and existing functions, the frozen rubric)
265	  plus a read-only export of the directories holding the two functions at the head commit,
266	  with read-only tools and no settings, memory or MCP. The export has no `.git`, so the
267	  labeler cannot read history or the PR outcome. This is the prereg's "repository, bodies,
268	  surrounding file" minus history. The model is `claude-opus-5-5`.
269	- **120-firing draw.** If more than 120 firings exist, 120 are drawn by seeded sample
270	  (seed 548) over firing ids alone, before any packet is built.
271	- **Git oracle, clarified.** Firings are computed at the PR's final head, so the ticket's
272	  "later PR revision" arm cannot apply by construction (the copy is present at head). Only
273	  the 6-month arm is measured, as the last default-branch commit within 183 days of the
274	  merge. A deleted or renamed file is `unscorable`, never counted as removed, so the oracle
275	  stays biased against the feature. Unmerged PRs are `unscorable`. It is reported and never
276	  decisive.
277	- **Sonar comparison is a proxy.** A firing counts as one Sonar would also fail only if it is
278	  an `exact` copy of at least 10 lines in a PR whose added functions in kept clusters exceed
279	  3% of the lines it added to Python files. This is not Sonar's 100-token detector.
280	- **Disk.** After the run, clones of repositories with no firings were deleted to free
281	  space. The ledger rows already carry everything the headroom figures need.
282	
283	### 2026-11-11, labeler A changed before the second labeler ran (tracked in #959)
284	
285	Thresholds, the firing definition, the rubric and the strict reading (both labelers TRUE)
286	are unchanged. One deviation from the pre-registered labeler pair, decided by the
287	maintainer and recorded here before the second labeler has run:
288	
289	- **Labeler A is a second fresh-context LLM, not the maintainer.** The pre-registration
290	  and its first addendum name the maintainer. The maintainer chose instead to run a second
291	  fresh-context LLM, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, as labeler A, on the same blind packets, with the
292	  same read-only export, tools and frozen rubric as labeler B (`claude-opus-5-5`). It has no
293	  access to labeler B's labels. **No human label exists for the primary oracle.**
294	- **What that weakens.** Two models from one vendor share training lineage, so shared blind
295	  spots are likelier than between a person and a model, and Cohen's kappa measures
296	  model-to-model agreement only. The results state this beside the headline number, and a
297	  pass is not described as human-validated.
298	- **Disclosure.** Three of labeler B's 119 labels were printed during an end-to-end check of
299	  the labeler, before this decision. They were not used to choose the second labeler, the
300	  model, or any threshold.
301	- **Optional spot-check.** A human label of a seeded subset may be added later, reported
302	  separately and never decisive. It would change no threshold.

# Pre-registration: does a diff-scoped "re-implemented an existing function" finding fire often enough, and is it right when it fires? (#548)

Written 2026-11-11, BEFORE `bench/diff_duplicates_precision.py` exists, before any PR was
drawn, and before any label was read. Edits after this date go in a dated addendum at the
bottom, never over this text. The commit that adds this file is quoted in the results.

## Question

`archy duplicates` reports the duplication backlog of a whole tree. A reviewer asks a
narrower thing at change time: did this diff add a function that already exists elsewhere?
Keeping only the clusters with one member inside the diff's added lines and one member that
already existed at the base commit would turn the report into that check. This study measures
two numbers on Python agent PRs before anything is built:

1. **Firing rate:** how many PRs produce at least one such cluster.
2. **Precision:** of the firings, how many are cases where the new function should have
   called or reused the existing one.

It measures the clones archy can see (AST-shape exact plus token-overlap near-miss). It does
not claim to cover Type-4 (semantic) redundancy, which is the kind the agent-PR literature
measures (arXiv 2601.21276) and which this detector misses by design. Low recall is expected
and is not a finding of this study.

No agent time is spent. The unit of work is a git checkout and a parse, so the expensive part
of any bench here (live agent runs) does not apply.

## The action, if it passes

The PR author or the agent is told "new `f` in `a/x.py` matches existing `b/y.f`" and deletes
the copy in favour of a call. If the study fails, nothing is built and
`docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md` records why. This ticket ships no CLI flag, MCP parameter or hook,
is never a score input, and adds no embeddings and no per-turn hook output.

## Prior art recorded before the run

- **SonarQube Cloud, "Sonar way for agentic AI"** already fails a PR whose new code has more
  than 3% duplicated lines. A Python duplicated block there needs at least 100 successive
  duplicated tokens over at least 10 lines, with only indentation and string literals
  ignored, so a copy with renamed identifiers is not a duplicate to Sonar. archy folds
  identifiers and literals. The gate is a density threshold, so one 15-line copy in a
  600-line PR (2.5%) passes. See "Reported, never decisive" for what this study records
  about it.
- **mick-gsk/drift** ships the in-loop version as a Claude Code hook and measures its own
  speak-rate by replay (0.0% to 5.6% on five repos). Its first run said 27% to 69% and the
  output was junk; the classes it derived are enumerated below so they are counted as
  reasons for FALSE labels instead of tuned away after the fact. Its replay measures noise,
  not precision or effect, so it does not change the anti-theater answer for this ticket.
- Detector precision history: about 50% similarity-only ceiling, about 63% exact tier, about
  74% source with co-change demotion (#242, #247, `docs/LEARNINGS.md`). Co-change abstains
  for files with fewer than 5 commits (`min_evidence`), so a copy in a NEW file falls back
  toward the ceiling. This study is expected to land nearer 50% than 74% for that reason.
- Two shipped detectors missed their pre-registered precision bars: Study 7 (0.024 against
  0.70) and Study 9 (0.215 against 0.40). Both harness bugs in Study 7 produced
  publishable-looking numbers, which is why the canary below runs before any real run.

## Population and sampling

- **Source:** AIDev (`hao-li/AIDev`), tables `pull_request` (state, `merged_at`, `repo_url`,
  `agent`) and `pr_commit_details` (`filename`, `status`, `patch`, per commit). The base
  commit and head commit of each PR are recovered from the repository's git history, not
  from the dataset.
- **Python PR:** a PR with at least one `.py` file whose patch carries an added line. Merged
  and closed-unmerged PRs are both in; open PRs are out (no outcome and the head moves).
- **Pilot:** 20 Python PRs drawn with seed 548. The pilot is disjoint from the main sample
  by construction (drawn first, removed from the pool).
- **Main sample:** N Python PRs drawn uniformly at random from the remaining pool with seed
  548 and at most 25 PRs per repository (the cap stops one prolific repository from
  supplying the whole firing set; it is applied in draw order). N is fixed in the
  post-pilot addendum from the pilot's measured wall time per PR, and only from that. The
  sample is not extended after the run starts: a short result is a result.
- **Unmeasurable PRs are dropped, never scored clean.** A PR whose base or head cannot be
  checked out, whose tree fails to parse, or whose scan exceeds the module cap is recorded
  with its reason and removed from the denominator. Dropped counts are reported by reason,
  and the headroom rate is also reported with every dropped PR counted as a non-firing, so
  the effect of dropping is visible.

## The detector and what counts as a firing

The shipped detector, unmodified, run on the head tree:

- exact clusters: `compute_duplicates(min_size=30)`, then `classify_variants`, then
  `demote_independent` where git history is present (the `archy duplicates` default);
- near-miss clusters: `compute_near_duplicates(min_size=30)` at the shipped 0.85 floor.
  These have no variant tier of their own, so the harness applies the same path filter
  (below) to them;
- **source-only (#247):** a cluster is dropped if any member is a test path
  (`is_test_path`) or a vendored path. Exact clusters the detector demotes to the `variant`
  tier are dropped. No other filter is added.

A cluster is a **firing** iff both hold, computed from `git diff base..head`:

- **A (new):** at least one member's `def` line falls inside an added hunk of the diff;
- **B (pre-existing):** at least one OTHER member existed at base, in a location outside the
  added hunks (a function present at base whose lines the diff did not add).

One firing is one (PR, cluster) pair. The unit of precision is the firing. Firings in one PR
are reported both ways (per firing and per PR) so a single PR cannot hide behind a count.
Only clusters the diff touches can fire, so a backlog cluster wholly at base never counts.

Headroom is `PRs with at least one firing / measured Python PRs`.

## Oracles

### Primary: blind labels from two labelers under the frozen rubric

Each scorable firing is labelled by two labelers working independently. Each sees the
repository, the new function and the existing function (paths, bodies, surrounding file),
and is blind to: the detector tier and similarity, the PR's merge outcome, the reviewers'
comments, and the git oracle. They label each firing TRUE or FALSE, and for FALSE record one
reason from the list below.

**TRUE** means: the new function should have called or reused the existing one (directly,
or by extracting a shared helper both call).

**FALSE** means: the duplication is intended or benign.

Frozen rubric for FALSE, one reason recorded per firing:

| reason | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sibling` | per-backend, per-provider, per-version or per-format siblings that differ in ways the shape folds away |
| `boilerplate` | property shims, one-line delegation, dunder methods, argument-parsing scaffolds, CLI or schema glue |
| `example-or-test-like` | examples, docs, scripts, fixtures, migrations or generated code restating a name by design (including paths the harness did not recognise as test or vendored) |
| `isolation` | deliberate independence: vendored or forked code, a layer that must not import the other |
| `same-class` | symmetric methods of one class or one protocol |
| `widespread-name` | the same shape appears in many places as a convention, so no single "existing one" exists to reuse |
| `short-or-trivial` | too small for reuse to be worth a call, despite clearing 30 nodes |
| `other` | free text, which the labeller must write |

A firing is **TRUE under the primary oracle only if both labelers say TRUE.** A split
decision is FALSE for the headline. The lenient reading (either says TRUE) is reported as
the upper bound and the strict reading as the headline; if they straddle a threshold, the
strict one decides. Cohen's kappa is reported with the counts. Labelers are recorded by
identity in the results; the labelling script reads nothing but the rubric and the two
functions.

If the firing set exceeds 120, a seeded draw (seed 548) of 120 is labelled, before anything
else is read. Below that, every firing is labelled.

**Firings that cannot be scored are dropped, never scored as clean.** A firing is
unscorable if either labeller cannot open the pre-existing member at its location, or the
two functions cannot be located at head. Drops are reported by reason.

### Secondary, reported and never decisive: the git oracle

A firing scores TRUE if the copy was removed or consolidated in a later revision of the same
PR or within 6 months on the default branch: the new function's qualified name is gone, or
its body no longer shares a shape with the existing member. The oracle is biased against the
feature, since reviewers do not object to redundant agent code (2601.21276), so it can only
under-count. It never decides a threshold.

### Reported, never decisive: the Sonar comparison

For each firing the primary oracle scores TRUE, record:

1. whether the copy is at least 10 lines and identifier-identical (byte-identical concrete
   body, which is the `exact` tier);
2. the PR's new-code duplicated-line density from the same added hunks. This is a PROXY:
   duplicated lines are the added lines of functions that are members of kept clusters, over
   all added lines in `.py` files. It is not Sonar's 100-token, 10-line detector and is
   labelled as a proxy wherever it appears.

If almost every TRUE firing would also have failed Sonar's 3% gate, the results say so,
because a follow-up feature would then add nothing for SonarQube users. The slice archy
alone would add is short copies, renamed copies, near-misses and copies diluted below 3% by
a large PR; any follow-up has to justify that slice. This adds no threshold.

## Thresholds

Fixed here, and not moved by the pilot or by anything read afterwards.

- **Headroom kill:** fewer than 1 firing per 50 Python agent PRs in the main sample (a rate
  below 2%), OR fewer than 30 scorable firings from at least 10 repositories. Either means
  the feature is not built. This is a result, not "underpowered, try again."
- **Precision pass:** at least 0.60 over at least 30 scorable firings from at least 10
  repositories, under the primary oracle.
- **Precision kill:** below 0.40.
- **Between 0.40 and 0.60:** null, and not shipped.

**No post-hoc subgroup rescues a null.** Exact versus near-miss, and new file versus
existing file, are reported in full, with counts and the reason breakdown, but they are not
results. The detector is not edited after the first labelled firing: the FALSE reasons above
are what a filter would have to remove, and removing them after seeing the labels would be
tuning on the test set.

## Process, in order

1. This document is committed. Its hash goes in the results.
2. The harness, the added-hunk unit tests (hand-built two-commit fixture; red when "member
   existed at base" is removed, red again when "def line inside an added hunk" is removed;
   the fixture asserts it contains a pre-existing match before asserting the outcome) and
   the canary.
3. `--canary`: a fixture PR that copies an existing function into a NEW file must fire, and a
   fixture PR that only edits an existing function must not. It runs before any real run.
4. Pilot on 20 disjoint PRs. **No labels are read.** It reports firing rate and harness bugs.
   A pilot of 20 expects well under one firing at a 2% rate, so it cannot estimate the rate
   and is a plumbing test only; the addendum says so. Its one design output is N, from
   wall time per PR.
5. Dated addendum fixing N, then the full run, resumable from the ledger (one row per PR,
   appended in a single write, only `status="ok"` counts as done, a crash in one PR does not
   end the run, stalls are retried and results never).
6. Labelling, then scoring against the thresholds, then
   `bench/diff_duplicates_precision_results.md` and a Study entry in
   `docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md`, published pass or fail.

## Descriptive extra, not a threshold

The headroom measurement already yields a speak-rate comparable to drift's replay numbers;
it is reported next to them so a reader can see whether archy would be noisier than the
in-loop tool that exists today.

## Addenda

### 2026-11-11, after the 20-PR pilot (no label read, no firing content read)

Thresholds, the firing definition and the rubric are unchanged. What the pilot fixed or
revealed:

- **Pilot result (counts only).** 20 PRs drawn, 7 measured, 9 had no added Python lines
  (dropped), 4 were dropped on `QualnameCollisionError`. 1 firing in 7 measured. As the
  plan said, this cannot estimate a rate near 2%; it is a plumbing test. Mean wall time was
  54 s per measured PR including cold clones. The pilot ledger is
  `bench/diff_duplicates_pilot.jsonl`; the pilot PRs are excluded from the main sample.
- **N = 2000.** The main sample is the 2000 PRs that follow the pilot in the seed-548
  shuffle, at most 25 per repository in draw order. About a third of draws are measurable
  in the pilot, so expect roughly 700 measured PRs; that expectation is an estimate from 20
  PRs and is not a commitment. The sample is not extended.
- **Pool is a proxy, the diff decides.** The draw pool is closed AIDev PRs in repositories
  whose AIDev `language` is Python (57,517 PRs in 4,255 repositories). A PR is a "Python
  PR" only if its own diff adds a `.py` line; the rest are dropped and recorded.
- **Diff base.** The base is `merge-base(PR base sha, PR head)`, the three-dot diff GitHub
  shows, so a PR branched long ago is not charged with unrelated base-branch changes. The
  head is the PR's `pull/N/head` ref.
- **Module-name collisions are dropped, not worked around.** 4 of the pilot's 11 Python PRs
  (prefect, mlflow, nexus and one more) hit `QualnameCollisionError`: archy refuses a tree
  where two files share a module name (#531), and the shipped CLI would refuse the same
  repositories. These are dropped and reported by reason, and the headroom rate is also
  reported with drops counted as non-firing. The results state plainly that this attrition
  falls on larger repositories, so the measured population leans toward smaller, cleaner
  ones. No fallback that ignores the colliding paths is added, since it would be a detector
  configuration the shipped CLI does not use.
- **Near-miss budget hits are flagged, not dropped.** The shipped near-miss pass stops at
  its 5,000,000-comparison budget and warns; at least one pilot repository hit it. A PR that
  hits it is still measured (the exact tier is complete) and its ledger row carries
  `near_miss_budget_hit`. The results report near-miss firings split by that flag, since a
  PR whose near-miss result may be short is not a clean negative for that tier.
- **Labelers.** Labeler A is the maintainer; labeler B is a fresh-context LLM given only
  the rubric and the two functions. Identities are recorded in the results.

### 2026-11-11, during the main run and before any label was read

Thresholds, the firing definition and the rubric are unchanged. Operational facts and two
clarifications, recorded before the results exist:

- **Analysis timeout is a drop.** One PR's analysis is run in a supervised child with a
  30 minute wall ceiling. The ceiling was added mid-run after a shard sat for 22 minutes on
  `git log -M` (the co-change layer) over a blobless clone of a very large repository. A PR
  that hits it is dropped with the reason `analysis timeout`, counted among the dropped
  Python PRs in the second headroom figure (drops counted as clean), and never as a clean
  PR. The affected shards were restarted on that code and resumed from their ledgers.
- **The run was sharded by repository** (8 workers), after the first 87 PRs ran in one
  process. The draw is unchanged and a PR's result does not depend on its shard.
- **Labeler B reads more than the packet.** It is a fresh-context `claude -p` run per
  firing, with the packet (repository, the new and existing functions, the frozen rubric)
  plus a read-only export of the directories holding the two functions at the head commit,
  with read-only tools and no settings, memory or MCP. The export has no `.git`, so the
  labeler cannot read history or the PR outcome. This is the prereg's "repository, bodies,
  surrounding file" minus history. The model is `claude-opus-5-5`.
- **120-firing draw.** If more than 120 firings exist, 120 are drawn by seeded sample
  (seed 548) over firing ids alone, before any packet is built.
- **Git oracle, clarified.** Firings are computed at the PR's final head, so the ticket's
  "later PR revision" arm cannot apply by construction (the copy is present at head). Only
  the 6-month arm is measured, as the last default-branch commit within 183 days of the
  merge. A deleted or renamed file is `unscorable`, never counted as removed, so the oracle
  stays biased against the feature. Unmerged PRs are `unscorable`. It is reported and never
  decisive.
- **Sonar comparison is a proxy.** A firing counts as one Sonar would also fail only if it is
  an `exact` copy of at least 10 lines in a PR whose added functions in kept clusters exceed
  3% of the lines it added to Python files. This is not Sonar's 100-token detector.
- **Disk.** After the run, clones of repositories with no firings were deleted to free
  space. The ledger rows already carry everything the headroom figures need.

### 2026-11-11, labeler A changed before the second labeler ran (tracked in #959)

Thresholds, the firing definition, the rubric and the strict reading (both labelers TRUE)
are unchanged. One deviation from the pre-registered labeler pair, decided by the
maintainer and recorded here before the second labeler has run:

- **Labeler A is a second fresh-context LLM, not the maintainer.** The pre-registration
  and its first addendum name the maintainer. The maintainer chose instead to run a second
  fresh-context LLM, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, as labeler A, on the same blind packets, with the
  same read-only export, tools and frozen rubric as labeler B (`claude-opus-5-5`). It has no
  access to labeler B's labels. **No human label exists for the primary oracle.**
- **What that weakens.** Two models from one vendor share training lineage, so shared blind
  spots are likelier than between a person and a model, and Cohen's kappa measures
  model-to-model agreement only. The results state this beside the headline number, and a
  pass is not described as human-validated.
- **Disclosure.** Three of labeler B's 119 labels were printed during an end-to-end check of
  the labeler, before this decision. They were not used to choose the second labeler, the
  model, or any threshold.
- **Optional spot-check.** A human label of a seeded subset may be added later, reported
  separately and never decisive. It would change no threshold.

# Pre-registration: what do the AST tiers miss that an embedding model finds on agent PRs? (#587)

Written 2026-11-12, BEFORE `bench/embedding_oracle_recall.py` exists, before any embedding was
computed, and before any label for this study was read. Edits after this date go in a dated
addendum at the bottom, never over this text. The commit that adds this file is quoted in the
results.

## Question

#548 measured the clones archy can see (AST-shape exact plus the token-overlap `near_miss`
tier) and found them 0.160 precise under two blind labelers (strict), below its 0.40 kill line
(`bench/diff_duplicates_precision_results.md`, Study 10). It did not measure Type-4 (semantic)
redundancy, which is the kind the agent-PR literature reports (arXiv 2601.21276) and which
those tiers miss by design. This study asks, offline and shipping nothing:

1. Of the added Python functions an embedding model pairs with a pre-existing function, how
   many are cases where the new function should have called or reused the existing one?
2. How much of the redundancy that people (here, two labelers) would act on is found only by
   the embedding model and not by the AST tiers?

It is research with a decision at the end. Nothing is added to the product, to `pyproject.toml`,
to `uv.lock`, to any CLI flag, MCP parameter or hook, or to the score. No agent time is spent;
the only cost is local CPU.

## What changed since the ticket was written

The ticket assumed #548 might ship a feature whose documentation #587 would then bound. #548
ended in a precision kill, so that feature is not built. Consequences, recorded here so they
are not discovered afterwards:

- Decision 3 in the ticket (state the AST share as the limit of #548's feature) is moot. The
  measured AST share is recorded instead as a limit on what the shipped `near_miss` and exact
  tiers can see, and nothing else.
- The AST tiers' strict precision is already known to be low (0.160). The pooled TRUE set is
  therefore expected to be small and to contain few pairs the AST tiers found. This makes the
  "at least 30% only by B" bar easier to clear than it looks, and is why a floor on the TRUE
  pool is added below. It is not a reason to move any bar.
- Any feature this study could justify would be a Type-4 tier, a separate feature with its own
  pre-registration, in a repository with fewer than 20 real users (usage baseline 2026-09-05).
  A pass files a ticket and builds nothing.

## The action, if it passes or fails

1. **Pass:** file a separate feature ticket for an opt-in Type-4 tier, to be pre-registered on
   its own. This ticket ships nothing.
2. **Kill:** record it in `docs/WHAT_DIDNT_WORK.md` and close the line so nobody re-proposes it.
3. **Null or not measurable:** record it, do not extend the sample after the run starts.

## Reused from #548, unchanged (no second harness)

- The AIDev pool, the seed-548 shuffle, the 20-PR pilot split (the pilot is excluded from
  everything below), and the per-repository cap.
- The set of **measured Python PRs** from #548's main run (1,049 PRs, ledger rows in
  `bench/diff_duplicates_data/precision.*.jsonl`). This study draws only from that set, so a PR
  is already known to clone, parse and scan, and A's firings for it already exist in the ledger.
  A PR that #548 dropped is not re-admitted. The population caveat from #548 carries over
  verbatim: module-name collisions dropped 22% of Python PRs, so the population may lean toward
  smaller, cleaner repositories.
- The firing definition for generator A, the source-only filter (`is_test_path`, vendored
  paths), the size floor (30 AST nodes, `MIN_NODES`), and the git base: `merge-base(PR base
  sha, PR head)` against the PR's `pull/N/head` ref.
- The frozen labeling rubric (TRUE definition and the eight FALSE reasons), the packet format,
